Team —

Quick kickoff for OrbitAI (ORB-2345). They expect a pilot close in the next 3 weeks and have asked for dedicated capacity guidance/ask so sales can finalize the commit. I pulled the attached pipeline snapshot and a proposed reserve model (sprint_reserve_model_v3.xlsx). Key numbers:

- Pilot expected ramp: 8k token-minute/day in week 1 -> 30k by week 4 (est.)
- Proposed committed baseline: 20 reserved slots (g5x-equivalent) with 50% burst pool access; peak burst need estimated at ~40 concurrent slots for short windows

Asks:
- Ben: confirm pool availability and provisioning lead time for 20 reserved slots (and how quickly we can scale to 40 if needed). See pool_availability_report.csv for current pool health (attached).
- Laura: sketch incremental monthly cost delta for 20 vs 40 committed slots and the revenue recognition timing considerations.
- Marissa / Jordan: ops/sales sequencing — if we ship a 20-slot commit now, what commitments do we need in contract language to enable burst credits?

Proposed timeline: finalize ask and legal/finance signoff by COB Jul 21 so infra can provision a reserved tranche by Jul 29. OrbitAI has agreed to a short sync — Megan is CC'd.

Attachments: sprint_reserve_model_v3.xlsx, orbitai_pipeline_snapshot.pdf

Thanks,
Kimberly Park

Kimberly —

Thanks for the summary and the model. Quick finance read:

- Committing to 20 reserved slots looks reasonable from a revenue/ARR perspective for the pilot, but we need to confirm contract term (3 vs 12 months) to model amortization. 3-month commitments materially increase unit cost.
- 40 committed slots would require a ~35% higher upfront commitment from OrbitAI; if they prefer elasticity, the burst-credit arrangement is the preferred path.

I attached a short cost delta worksheet (finance_impact_estimate.xlsx) with the two scenarios. Action items for us:
- Kimberly: confirm expected contract term (they indicated pilot + option to extend).
- Sales: include explicit burst credit mechanics (how many credits, replenishment cadence) so we can model variable revenue recognition.

If OrbitAI can agree to a 6-month minimum on the 20-slot base, finance will greenlight the lower-unit-cost scenario and approve billing cadence.

—Laura

Looping infra context in —

We ran the pool health check this morning. Highlights (see attached pool_availability_report.csv):
- Current G5x-equivalent committed utilization: 72% across reserved pools this quarter; cold start buffer ~6 slots in primary US-west pool.
- We can allocate 20 reserved slots within 7–10 business days if we prioritize capacity and pull from burst buffer; provisioning to 40 persistent reserved slots would need ~3 weeks lead time and requires confirming long-lived commit.

Fallbacks and mitigations:
- We can set up a reserved baseline on g5x and configure overflow routing to quantized variants (g5q) for non-critical low-latency jobs to reduce unit cost during bursts.
- If OrbitAI needs immediate peak headroom, we suggest a short-term burst escrow (pre-purchased credits) that can be consumed while reserved capacity is being provisioned.

Proposed infra timeline if approved by COB Jul 21: provision 20 reserved slots by Jul 29, enable burst-escrow on Jul 29, target full 40 reserved tranche by Aug 12 if they commit to extension.

Ben Carter
Director, Infrastructure Capacity
